title: SaveChanges and transactions
summary: All or nothing: one SaveChanges is a transaction, and BeginTransaction groups several.

steps.title: One save, one transaction
body: `SaveChanges` sends every pending change **inside a database transaction**. If any statement fails (a constraint, a lost connection), the database rolls back all of them. You never get half a save.
That covers most needs: put everything that belongs together into the context, then save once.

> **Tip:** After a failed `SaveChanges`, the entities are still in the context with their changes. Fix them, or call `db.ChangeTracker.Clear()` before reusing the context, or the next save retries the same failing change.

steps.prompt: What does this print? (`Balance` has a check constraint: it may not go below 0.)
code: seed.Accounts.AddRange(new Account { Owner = "Ana", Balance = 100 }, new Account { Owner = "Ben", Balance = 20 });
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=bank.db");
steps.explain: Ben would go to -30, which the check constraint refuses. Because both updates were in one transaction, Ana's +50 was rolled back too. Money is neither created nor lost.

steps.title: Several saves, one transaction
body: Sometimes you need **two** `SaveChanges` calls to succeed or fail together: for example, you need the generated id from the first save to build the second. Wrap them in an explicit transaction:
If anything throws before `Commit`, disposing `tx` (the end of the `using`) **rolls back** both saves. You can also call `tx.Rollback()` yourself.

steps.prompt: Arrange a transfer done with two saves, so that both happen or neither does.
steps.explain: The transaction must begin before the first save, and commit only after the last one succeeded.

code: seed.Accounts.AddRange(new Account { Owner = "Ana", Balance = 100 }, new Account { Owner = "Ben", Balance = 20 });
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=bank.db");
steps.explain: Both saves ran inside the transaction, and both succeeded, but `Rollback` undid them: Cy was never created and Ana keeps her 100.

options: When several `SaveChanges` calls (or raw SQL commands) must succeed or fail as one
steps.explain: A single `SaveChanges` is already atomic. Explicit transactions are for grouping several of them, or mixing them with `ExecuteSql`, `ExecuteUpdate` and the like.

steps.prompt: Complete the code so a failure anywhere undoes both saves.
steps.explain: `BeginTransaction` opens it and `Commit` makes it permanent. Without `Commit`, disposing the transaction rolls everything back.

steps.title: A safe transfer
prompt: The tests give you `BankDb` with `Accounts` (`Id`, `Owner`, `Balance`) and a check constraint that `Balance >= 0`.
Write `bool Transfer(BankDb db, int fromId, int toId, int amount, List<string> log)`:
2. Take `amount` from the source account and **save**.
4. Give `amount` to the target account and **save**.
If any save fails, roll back, clear the change tracker, and return `false` (the log line may stay, but **no money may move**).
starter: bool Transfer(BankDb db, int fromId, int toId, int amount, List<string> log)
solution: bool Transfer(BankDb db, int fromId, int toId, int amount, List<string> log)
template: seed.Accounts.AddRange(new Account { Owner = "Ana", Balance = 100 }, new Account { Owner = "Ben", Balance = 20 }, new Account { Owner = "Vault", Balance = 2147483600 });
Dojo.Eq("Ana sends Ben 40", true, Transfer(dojoDb, 1, 2, 40, dojoLog));
Dojo.Eq("Ben cannot send 500", false, Transfer(dojoDb, 2, 1, 500, dojoLog));
Dojo.Eq("an overflowing credit fails after the debit was saved", false, Transfer(dojoDb, 1, 3, 50, dojoLog));
Dojo.Eq("only the first transfer moved money", "Ana=60 Ben=60 Vault=2147483600", string.Join(" ", dojoDb.Accounts.OrderBy(a => a.Id).Select(a => a.Owner + "=" + a.Balance)));
Dojo.Check("the debit of the failed third transfer was logged before it was undone", dojoLog.Contains("debit 1 50"), string.Join(", ", dojoLog));
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=bank.db");
